segments.text: This is our Baxter picking up a red cube. Force pads under its fingers report contact two hundred times a second. When the gripper closes, the signal jumps from ninety-two counts to over four hundred.
segments.visual: Successful ACT rollout (rollouts ep 0), head camera at half speed, wrist camera inset, the 200 Hz pad trace drawing in sync underneath.

segments.text: Tactile Flora. Teaching robots to tell when they failed.
segments.visual: Title card over a dimmed freeze frame of the lifted cube.

segments.text: Learned policies fail quietly. Our ACT policy succeeded once in ten runs on the real robot. Eight of the nine failures were safety aborts: a new action chunk started more than a quarter radian from where the arm actually was. Someone has to watch every run, and the camera often misses the moment that matters, because the gripper hides the contact.
segments.visual: Four failed rollouts looping in a grid, the real run log with stop reasons, the 1 of 10 tally.

segments.text: So we built three pieces. Force pads on Baxter's gripper, streamed at two hundred hertz. Tactile Flora: NVIDIA's twenty-seven billion parameter video reward model, which we fine-tuned to judge success from video plus force. And a Pi zero point five policy, fine-tuned for this arm.
segments.visual: System diagram: sense, judge, act, each card lighting up with its own footage.

segments.text: We fine-tuned Flora on over eighteen hundred real manipulation clips and tested it once, on four hundred twenty-eight locked trials with fifty-nine unseen objects. Failure-detection AUROC rose from 0.783 to 0.956. Failure recall went from thirty-four to eighty-four percent, while still passing ninety-eight percent of successes. On Reassemble, AUROC rose from 0.648 to 0.919.
segments.visual: HRDexDB footage beside an ROC chart that builds curve by curve, then the headline numbers.

segments.text: Then the honest surprise. At Flora's native video resolution, force added nothing measurable: a matched model without force scored 0.964. When the model saw ninety-six pixel thumbnails, force added 0.043. Touch matters where vision is starved. And force alone, with no video, already reaches 0.75 to 0.82.
segments.visual: A v3 clip where force fixed the call, then the force gain at 96 px versus native resolution, and the force-only classifier.

segments.text_template: We fine-tuned Pi zero point five overnight on a laptop GPU, from eighteen kinesthetic demonstrations. The vision-language backbone stays frozen, matching its knowledge-insulation training, and low-rank adapters train the action expert. Actions are relative to the current joint state, so every chunk is anchored to where the arm actually is. On two held-out demonstrations, {result_sentence}

segments.text: Tactile Flora gives a robot a judge that catches its failures, and a sense of touch where its eyes fall short. Code, data, and results are open at github dot com slash ogershony slash tactile flora.
